Mahindra Vision S Two Test Mules At Traffic Stop

KS
By Kabir Sharma Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist • via Rushlane.com Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Rushlane.com Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Two camouflaged Mahindra Vision S test mules have been spotted together in Hyderabad after dark.
  • The latest spy shots, shared by automotive enthusiast Abhiram, give us a close look at the front lighting and grille of the upcoming compact SUV .
  • They also show the Scorpio-style rear pillar lamps and the lower tail lamps illuminated on the same prototype, bringing together details seen in separate sightings earlier this year.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • KABIR SHARMA Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist

Bharat NCAP Safety Standards & Indian Road Readiness

In India's rapidly evolving automotive landscape, crashworthiness and real-world durability are driving consumer purchase decisions like never before. As reported by Rushlane.com, indigenous automakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra are setting global safety benchmarks while optimizing suspension and ground clearance for unpredictable road conditions.

Big Picture: Upcoming monthly FADA retail delivery reports and Bharat NCAP rating scorecards will reveal which domestic models capture mass-market dominance.

Two camouflaged Mahindra Vision S test mules have been spotted together in Hyderabad after dark. The latest spy shots, shared by automotive enthusiast Abhiram, give us a close look at the front lighting and grille of the upcoming compact SUV . They also show the Scorpio-style rear pillar lamps and the lower tail lamps illuminated on the same prototype, bringing together details seen in separate sightings earlier this year.

📌 The Core Development

Both prototypes have an upright front end with six vertical grille openings, arranged in two groups of three. Horizontal slats are visible inside the openings, while the bumper has a pair of wide rectangular cutouts below the grille.

Much of the front remains wrapped, but the outline is consistent with the upright nose and six-slot grille shown in the Vision S design patent we covered in October. The night shots offer a clearer view of the lighting around the outer edges of the front fascia.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Each side has a bright upper lamp, a short horizontal light element extending towards the grille and a vertical illuminated section along the outer edge. Close-ups also show smaller modules stacked beneath the upper lamp within the rectangular housing.

The side views show the flat roofline, squared wheel arches and short rear overhang, with the spare wheel mounted on the tailgate. Both test vehicles use conventional door mirrors, a detail that distinguishes them from the camera-based units shown in the concept patent . The Hyderabad photos follow an earlier sighting shared by automotive enthusiast Joshua, who spotted a camouflaged prototype near Uthukottai.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

A rear-quarter close-up shows a stack of red segments illuminated high on the rear pillar, alongside the rear windscreen. Below it, a separate lamp assembly lights up next to the spare wheel. The upper placement recalls the Scorpio Classic and Scorpio N, while the lower cluster includes a short horizontal section that extends inwards towards the tailgate.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

The production SUV is expected to use Mahindra’s modular NU_IQ architecture and target the sub-four-metre segment . Earlier test mules revealed two horizontal displays, vertical AC vents and an electronic parking brake. The latest exterior photographs add a clearer view of the body and lighting, while the final cabin and equipment list are still awaited.

A 1.2-litre turbo petrol and a 1.5-litre diesel are possible engine options. Mahindra has confirmed that the architecture supports combustion and electric powertrains, with the production Vision S lineup yet to be announced. A launch is scheduled in H1 2027. It is likely to slot between the XUV 3XO (price range Rs 7.8 lakh to Rs 15 lakh) and Thar OG (Rs 10.32 lakh to Rs 19 lakh) in the company lineup.
